assertion_analysis.failure_condition: The diff adds no assertion; it makes pre-existing ones load-bearing. This assertion requires the session-wide render of a B row (own entry 1) to contain " 8w  2h  3d" (7 from A + 1 from B). It fails if _session_counts_in_other_projects or the latest-transition selection lets C's older entry of 5 in (rendering 13w) or drops the other project's figure; nc_broken.log shows exactly that failure at this line. It compares a literal against the code's render, not against a value the test fed in, so it is independent of the value under test.

This is the C clause the plan names: _scoped_watch_event(a_row, SESSION) must report working==8 with a literal 8 against the code output, so it fails if C's older 5 is summed. Before the change it could not fail on the selection, because C unpublished made _other_project_producer_is_live exclude C whatever _newest_session_event returned (repro_c_clause_unpublished.log: base test + mutation = 1 passed). After the change it can, but the negative control never reaches it: line 136 reddens first on the same mutation.

The unscoped render of a B row (built from _entry(1)) must contain " 1w  0h  0d" and must not contain " 8w". The value 1 originates in the row the test built, but the guard is on the transform (an unscoped row keeps its own project's figures instead of summing), so a regression that summed across projects for a sessionless follower would make the membership fail; it is not an identity assertion.

No assertion guards this line. Removing _publish("C", SESSION) leaves the whole test green (repro_c_clause_unpublished.log shows the base test with the selection mutated still reports 1 passed), so the clause's sensitivity to the newest-transition selection is silently disarmed if this line is reverted.

0.reason: the mutation reddens the file, so the newest-transition selection is guarded; the landing record states that the earlier render assertion is the one that fails

findings.text: follow-on: the negative control fails on the pre-existing cross-project render assertion at line 136, not on the C clause (lines 142-145) the plan names; logs/nc_broken.log shows the B row rendering " 13w  2h  3d" against the literal " 8w  2h  3d" at line 136. The landing line and the fragment both state "the C clause fails", which is a claim the recorded log does not show — the C clause's own assertions never execute under the mutation because line 136 reddens first. The substance of the deliverable is met (the mutation is caught and renders 13w), but the record overstates which assertion caught it.

follow-on: the added _publish("C", SESSION) is itself unguarded. Nothing asserts C's producer is published, and the run's own repro log proves that with C unpublished the selection mutation goes undetected (1 passed, EXIT=0), so reverting this one line returns the file to green while the clause it was added to arm loses its sensitivity. The guard against the regression this node exists to catch can be silently removed with no failing test.
